analysis.title: Fed signals keep fixed income under pressure
key_insights: Rates rose sharply in the week to 13 Nov 2026 after October U.S. CPI came in hotter than expected and Fed commentary turned more hawkish. Governor Waller suggested a 50 basis point hike should be considered in December.

Fixed income losses were broad and nearly all rate-driven. The Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate returned -1.50% on the week and the U.S. Treasury Index -1.45%. Taxable municipals (-1.96%) and agency MBS (-1.84%) fell most because of their duration.
Floating-rate assets were the exception. Senior loans returned +0.21%, CLO AA +0.10% and CLO BB +1.17% on the week. Convertibles rose with equities.
Credit spreads tightened across investment grade, high yield and emerging markets even as rates sold off, so the losses came from duration and not from credit.

Treasury yields rose across the curve and erased several weeks of gains. Short maturities moved most and the curve flattened: 2-year +33 bps to 4.84%, 5-year +32 bps to 4.96%, 10-year +28 bps to 5.14%, 20-year +22 bps to 5.52%, 30-year +20 bps to 5.47%.

Nuveen says markets fully price a December Fed hike and more hikes in early 2027, a more aggressive path than its own. It expects one more hike by year-end, then a hold through 2027. The view depends on the energy shock and its pass-through to core inflation.

Nuveen forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% for year-end 2026 and 4.75% for end-2027, and the 2-year at 4.70% this year and 4.50% next year. The 10-year closed the week at 5.14%, above its year-end forecast.
Municipals fell less than Treasuries because muni yields rose less than the Treasury curve. Nuveen continues to favor longer duration in municipals over Treasuries.

Taxable municipals were the weakest sector because of their long maturity profile. Nuveen sees higher absolute yields attracting crossover buyers and views the backup as a potential opportunity to earn income.
Investment grade spreads tightened broadly across ratings and sectors, supported by expectations of lighter supply into year-end. Fund inflows slowed in a holiday-shortened week.
High yield declined only modestly (-0.26%) as tighter spreads cushioned the rate move. Issuance was light and activity was driven by earnings and company-specific news.
Preferreds fell as yields rose, though spreads tightened. Retail-oriented par preferreds lagged, extending a difficult year, while bank and European issues held up better.

Agency MBS underperformed as their yield premium over Treasuries widened toward a one-year high. Securitized credit held up better, with consumer ABS issuance well received and CLOs firm as investors favored floating-rate assets ahead of likely further hikes.

Emerging markets debt fell with global rates. Hard currency spreads tightened and corporates outperformed sovereigns, while local currency lagged as the dollar strengthened. Investor outflows accelerated.
Equities were volatile but finished higher after the prior week's AI-led selloff. A leadership change at a major semiconductor firm weighed on the sector late in the week.

sector_views.rationale: Favors longer duration in municipals over Treasuries because yields remain near levels that have historically attracted buyers.
Higher absolute yields should attract crossover buyers, and the backup is seen as a potential opportunity to earn attractive income.
Credit fundamentals remain sound, reinforced by spreads tightening through the selloff. Nuveen continues to favor high-quality income.

macro_indicators.reading: Hotter than expected, no figure given in this report
macro_indicators.interpretation: The hot October print, together with hawkish Fed commentary, pushed Treasury yields sharply higher and raised expectations for further tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: Markets fully price a hike. Governor Waller suggested a 50 bp hike should be considered.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is more aggressive than Nuveen's forecast of one more hike by year-end.

macro_indicators.reading: One more hike by year-end 2026, then a hold through 2027 (Nuveen forecast)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Nuveen expects fewer hikes than markets price, and the view depends on energy shock pass-through to core inflation.
Up 28 bps on the week, 21 bps month-to-date and 97 bps year-to-date.
Both forecasts sit below the current 5.14% level.
The 2-year closed the week at 4.84%, above the 2026 forecast.
Up 33 bps on the week. Short maturities moved most, which flattened the curve.

trade_ideas.description: Favor longer duration in municipals over Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Muni yields rose less than Treasury yields and remain near levels that have historically attracted buyers.

risk_factors: Further hawkish Fed repricing, including a 50 bp December hike and additional hikes in early 2027.
The energy shock passing through to core inflation, which Nuveen's one-more-hike-then-hold view depends on.
Duration exposure: taxable municipals, agency MBS and long-dated Treasuries are most exposed to rising yields.
Accelerating outflows from emerging markets debt and a stronger dollar for local currency markets.
vol_and_positioning: Investor outflows from emerging markets debt accelerated, while new issuance met solid demand.
Fund inflows into investment grade slowed in a U.S. holiday-shortened week. Loan fund flows stayed positive.
Retail-oriented par preferreds continued to lag, while bank and European preferreds held up better.
Investors favored floating-rate assets such as CLOs ahead of likely further Fed hikes.
geopolitical: The report refers to an energy shock and its pass-through to core inflation as the key dependency for the Fed outlook.

tension_points.bull_case: Nuveen expects only one more hike by year-end followed by an extended hold through 2027, which is less aggressive than market pricing and leaves room for yields to ease toward its 10-year forecast of 4.95% for year-end 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets fully price a December hike and additional hikes in early 2027, and Governor Waller suggested a 50 bp December hike should be considered. Hot October CPI supports the more aggressive path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy shock pass-through to core inflation, which Nuveen says its view depends on. FOMC minutes are due the week of 16 Nov.
